card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 11 That Randomly Restarts

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 11 That Randomly Restarts

claims.statement: iPhone 11 Missing sensors TG0B/TG0V = battery or battery data lines; diode-check I2C2_SMC_SCL_CONN and I2C2_SMC_SDA_CONN.
If those battery data pins read OL, check resistors R3202 and R3201; otherwise the break may be under the CPU (reball). A short points to caps around the connector or an unfixable CPU fault.
Prs0/Mic1 = charging port flex; also check R6822 (I2C1_AOP_SCL), R6823 (I2C1_AOP_SDA) and volume flex oxidation.
Mic2 = power button flex mic; an OL at the power button connector after a hard drop can mean sandwich separation needing a reball.

procedure: Read Missing sensors in the latest panic-full log.
TG0B/TG0V: battery swap; diode-check SMC I2C pins; check R3201/R3202.
Prs0/Mic1: known-good charge flex; check R6822/R6823; inspect volume flex.
Mic2: known-good power button flex; diode-check its connector; reball sandwich if OL.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
card.component: Battery / charge port flex / power button flex
